messages.author: 51f4f7851e64fd7f
messages.subject: snapclust
parts:
Hi Dr. Kamvar and all, 

It is me again troubling you with a code in adegenet. I cannot find a group for adegent. So I thought post here and get some advice for my issue.

I conducted my analyses using poppr and adegent (Clone correction, AMOVA, DAPC etc.) for my haploid and dominate DArT data set which is in Genalex format (Presence 1, Absence 0, Missing -1 ). 

I want to find out clusters in my population using snapclust command. However, when I run the following code I always get an error message.  

Code

a.aic <- snapclust.choose.k(max = 15, genchar)         

Error message

Error in FUN(newX[, i], ...) : arguments must have same length 

Then I changed my file format into different formats like text, excel and csv, also I changed the allele names  (Presence 1, Absence 2, Missing 0 ) but still I could not figure out the problem.

I would be grateful to you, if you could advice me. 

Thank you.

Best regards
Buddhika

messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: [poppr] snapclust
parts:
Hi Buddhika,

This is a bug in snapclust, but I don't know how soon it can be fixed since the maintainer of adegenet is currently in the DRC assisting with the Ebola epidemic at the moment. Additionally, snapclust was developed with codominant markers in mind, so it's not clear what the ramifications of using it on dominant markers would be (though I suspect the effect is NIL).

Best,
Zhian

messages.subject: Re: [poppr] snapclust
parts:
Hi Dr. Kamvar, 

I am trying to correlate the genetic distances of my seven populations with the locations that they have been collected. I am working with "mantel test" for this purpose and I use following commands. 

commands

genchar_dists <- dist(genchar@other$xy, method="euclidean")

genchar.pw_D <- pairwise_D(genchar, linearized=TRUE)

mantel.rtest(genchar.pw_D, log(genchar_dists), 999) 

Whenever I run these codes I get this error message. 

> mantel.rtest(genchar.pw_D, log(genchar_dists), 999)
Error in if (any(distmat < tol)) warning("Zero distance(s)") : 
  missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed


I realised that my pairwise distances among locations cannot be found out by "pairwise_D" command as it always results distances as  "NaN" .

 I am truly sorry to bother with frequent questions. 

Best regards
Buddhika

As none of these functions are from poppr and I don't particularly know what pairwise_D does or what it returns (I can only assume a distance matrix), I'm afraid I cannot help with this situation. I would suggest to contact the maintainer of the package that pairwise_D comes from and ask them why you are getting NaN values.

Best,
Zhian
